voci.titolo: Warsh wants the Fed to say less. Two officials are pushing for more transparency.
voci.riassunto: More interest-rate hikes are needed to fight inflation, Fed officials say.

voci.titolo: Wall Street Boom to Cut New York State Budget Deficit in Half
voci.riassunto: New York projected the budget deficit will narrow by $3.5 billion next year as the state expects a boom in trading and borrowing to deliver record profits to Wall Street and stronger bonus payments to boost revenue.

voci.titolo: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts
voci.riassunto: The euro zone showed surprising resilience, but weak productivity, industrial competitiveness challenges and demographic pressures remain, analysts said.

voci.titolo: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates
voci.riassunto: The personal consumption expenditures price index was projected to increase 0.5% in September for an annual rate of 3.7%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

voci.titolo: Analysis: Kevin Warsh is keeping Wall Street guessing. It may be his most powerful tool
voci.riassunto: The new chairman made clear he leans toward higher interest rates, but left himself options depending on how the data comes in.

voci.titolo: The politics of President Lagarde's European Central Bank early exit — and who could replace her
voci.riassunto: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on Feb. 7 next year, she announced Thursday.

voci.titolo: European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%
voci.riassunto: Markets saw the decision as a hawkish pause and were last pricing in a 67% chance of a December rate hike.

voci.titolo: Here are five key takeaways from the Fed rate decision and Warsh news conference
voci.riassunto: Even though the interest-rate vote went as expected, there were a few surprises out of this week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

voci.titolo: Bessent says 'not necessarily' a mistake if the Fed hikes again
voci.riassunto: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined CNBC for an interview on Oct. 28, 2026.

voci.titolo: The UK cuts energy bills, taxes banks and boosts defense in high-stakes budget
voci.riassunto: The U.K. budget cuts household energy costs, raises taxes on banks and directs billions toward defense, Ukraine and artificial intelligence

voci.titolo: World Bank's Banga: Availability of capital 'not really an issue' as AI demand drives up borrowing costs
voci.riassunto: World Bank President Ajay Banga came on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 27, 2026.

voci.titolo: Fed rate hikes are coming, but not this week: CNBC survey
voci.riassunto: The CNBC Fed Survey shows that 93% of respondent expect a pause at the Federal Reserve meeting taking place this week.

voci.titolo: Analysis: Why a $2 trillion deficit and 5% Treasury yields are becoming America's biggest economic challenge
voci.riassunto: Treasury yields above 5% are raising borrowing costs for households and the federal government, highlighting the challenge of financing $2 trillion deficits.

voci.titolo: Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey
voci.riassunto: Eight out of 10 Americans now rate the economy as fair or poor, one of several findings in a CNBC poll that show why Republican candidates face uphill battles.

voci.titolo: Jobless claims near the lowest since the 1960s as low-fire trend continues
voci.riassunto: Initial filings for unemployment insurance slipped to a seasonally adjusted 194,000.

voci.titolo: Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes
voci.riassunto: Housing data deteriorated further in September, according to separate reports Tuesday.

voci.titolo: UK inflation jumps to 3.5% — cementing rate hike expectations
voci.riassunto: U.K. inflation rose by a hotter-than-expected 3.5% in the 12 months to September, driven by the surging cost of motor fuels.

voci.titolo: Car buyers are demanding lower prices and better tech. Automakers must deliver both
voci.riassunto: Bain says tech leads purchase considerations in China while price remains No. 1 in the U.S. and Europe, as pressure mounts on Western carmakers.
